newsitem.title: BOSNIA: German, French defence ministers visit Bosnia.
newsitem.headline: German, French defence ministers visit Bosnia.

text.p: German and French defence ministers travelled to Bosnia on Monday to check on preparations for the deployment of a Franco-German contingent which will serve in the NATO-led peacekeeping force.

After flying into Sarajevo airport, Germany's Volker Ruehe and his French counterpart Charles Millon met German officers involved in planning the first deployment of German combat units abroad since World War Two.

Some 3,000 German soldiers, sailors and airmen will join the NATO-led stabilisation force in January to help enforce the peace agreeement in former Yugoslavia, where memories of atrocities committed by Hitler's Nazis are still alive.

A German force of 2,000, part of a Franco-German brigade based in Germany, will move into Bosnia itself and will serve under French command in the southeast region around the town of Mostar, inside Moslem-Croat federation territory.
The German troops will arrive with Luchs armoured reconaissance vehicles equipped with 20 mm machine guns as well as armoured personnel carriers.
But the Germans, sensitive to stirring up memories of World War Two, will not be driving tanks in Bosnia, NATO officers said.
An advance team of some 70 German officers is already in Sarajevo preparing for the arrival of the combat units in January.
Some 4,000 German military personnel in logistics, engineering and medical units are currently serving in ex- Yugoslavia in the NATO-led mission.

As defence minister, Ruehe has led efforts to gradually remove the taboo on German troops serving abroad, culminating in a vote by the German parliament this month approving the use of combat troops in the Balkans.
Hitler's army attacked Yugoslavia on April 6, 1941, and occupied the country until 1945.
Nazi units brought the holocaust to Yugoslavia, conducting mass shootings of Jewish men and sending Jewish women and children to their deaths in gas chambers in 1942.
